items.title: Joe Watkins Interview, 1961-01-20
items.q: Well we had Talbot, Slow Drag, Elton Pornell, George Lewis, Lawrence Moreira and myself. That was the old regular lineup.

ctx.x: Well we worked there for a couple of years. Who do you have in the band then?
Well we had Talbot, Slow Drag, Elton Pornell, George Lewis, Lawrence Moreira and myself. That was the old regular lineup.

items.title: Joe Watkins Interview, 1969-03-24
items.q: That was including Elton Pennell, Slow Drag, Lawrence, and myself.

ctx.x: Let me ask you about playing with the George Lewis band and what sort of a band you thought it was and how you played and how you particularly yourself played.

Well, I'll tell you, Tom. George Lewis wanted the best or nothing at all. And he did get that recognition for his rhythm section. He was supposed to have the best rhythm section on it. That was including Elton Pennell, Slow Drag, Lawrence, and myself. And when he got that, he was satisfied. But, he wants you to keep that drive. See, that was a driving beat that he had me working on. That wasn't exactly what you would call an authentic jazz beat. See? Because if you listen plainly to Saeed, you don't hear that…
Did George give you any particular instructions as to how he wanted you to play?

items.title: Alcide "Slow Drag" Pavageau and Lawrence Marrero Interview, 1957-09-01
items.q: we had one of the best rhythm sessions they had. George Moods, George Moods, yeah. Elton Pointer, and Joe Watkins on the drums.

ctx.x: Yes I do. And we had, I'll tell you, we had one of the best rhythm sessions they had. George Moods, George Moods, yeah. Elton Pointer, and Joe Watkins on the drums. Yeah, we had one of the best rhythm sessions I think they had on. Yeah. Well see my banjo playing is cold and heavy comp. And when they tell me to get off, I get off. That's where I do it now. That's where the people, these people take a light to my playing because I play it different from everybody. I'm trying to get up there and try to play solo,…
You make a couple of chords, not strum them, but just finger them. I'd like to see how your fingers... Do you want to finger on a chord? Do you want anything?

items.title: Joe Watkins Interview, 1960-03-16
items.q: That was the last time Lawrence played out there with us.

ctx.x: Yeah, baby used to have to do that and after you had it, you couldn't move it fast.

No, I noticed that because he had wrestled me up several times at the hunt club in Chicago. He used to come there and ask about the wrestling up. I said, man, I said, you're doing me all the good in the world. I said, they sit out in that audience and look at you sitting up on my drums. I said, it makes me feel good, baby. One night I cried, I'm telling you the truth. I really broke down and cried, you know, to see how he was up there fighting, you know, to try to get his arms in shape, you know. And I said,…
